name: rushes

attributes.attribute: dressed in rags with a turnip head
carried on the eve of Brigit's day
ancient Celtic feast of Brigit's day

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Rushes made up a festival doll. People bound them to form the body. A second bundle formed the hands. They dressed the figure in rags. Some used a broom or churn-dash. A turnip served as the head. On the eve of Brigit's day, the feast of Imbolc, children carried the doll. They went door to door asking coins for poor Biddy. Unmarried girls carried it in many places. The doll was the brideog, or little Brigit.

okr.objective: The brideog is a rush doll of the Imbolc festival.
key_results: The brideog is a doll made from bound rushes.
Children carried it on the eve of Brigit's day.
That eve was the feast of Imbolc.
Only unmarried girls carried it in some villages.
